system_description.narrative_title: U.S.–Iran hostilities at the Strait of Hormuz disrupting oil and markets
system_description.narrative_summary: Renewed U.S.–Iran military exchanges centered on the Strait of Hormuz — including attacks on tankers, mine warfare claims and U.S. strikes on Iranian targets — are the dominant story, driving oil-price spikes, shipping disruptions and market volatility. Described as an open system, the episode links heterogeneous actors (U.S., Iran, Gulf states, shipping companies, OPEC+, insurers, markets), material and informational flows (oil shipments, strikes, sanctions, news), and dynamic feedbacks (attacks → reduced transits → higher oil prices → inflation/market moves → political and policy responses that can amplify or dampen further action), with important time lags between measures (sanctions/blockade) and their economic effects. Boundaries are porous: localized maritime insecurity propagates across global energy supply chains, financial markets and regional politics, creating spillovers and systemic risk.
system_description.scope: Maritime security in and around the Strait of Hormuz, tanker attacks and mining, U.S.–Iran military strikes and reprisals, oil shipment flows and OPEC+/export responses, sanctions/blockade measures, market (oil, gold, bonds, equities) and insurance reactions.
system_description.super_system: Global economic and security system (international energy security, trade and financial markets).
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil market and OPEC+ production policy
Financial markets (commodities, bonds, FX, equities) and central-bank policy
Regional geopolitics and U.S. domestic politics (electoral timing, sanctions policy)

variables.name: Maritime transit volume
variables.description: Rate of commercial vessel transits through the relevant maritime corridor measured in vessel-count or tonnage per unit time.

variables.name: Maritime security incident rate
variables.description: Frequency of security-related incidents (attacks, collisions, mine strikes, interdictions) affecting commercial navigation per unit time.

variables.name: Naval/military operational intensity
variables.description: Overall level of military naval operations and kinetic activity in the maritime theatre, including patrols, strikes and countermeasures.

variables.name: Mine presence density
variables.description: Concentration of naval mines and similar denial devices in the operational area measured per unit area or per sea lane segment.

variables.name: Tanker fleet availability
variables.description: Proportion of tanker fleet capacity available and operational for long-haul crude or product shipments at a given time.

variables.name: Oil shipment throughput
variables.description: Volume flow of crude and refined petroleum transported through the maritime route measured in barrels per unit time.

variables.name: Global oil price level
variables.description: Market price per barrel for benchmark crude reflecting global supply-demand balance and risk premia.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium level
variables.description: Average cost of hull and war-risk insurance for vessels operating in the region, expressed as a premium rate or surcharge.

variables.name: Market volatility level
variables.description: Degree of short-term price variability and uncertainty across relevant asset markets (commodities, equities, bonds) as measured by volatility metrics.

variables.name: Supply chain delay index
variables.description: Average additional transit and logistics delay imposed on energy and commodity supply chains due to route changes, inspections or disruptions.

variables.name: Spare production capacity
variables.description: Aggregate unused production capacity in the global oil supply system that can be brought online within a defined timeframe.

variables.name: Export infrastructure utilization
variables.description: Percentage utilization of export facilities, terminals and chokepoint throughput capacity relative to maximum operating capability.

variables.name: Financial market liquidity
variables.description: Ease and depth with which market participants can buy or sell relevant financial instruments without large price impact.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: Average anticipated future inflation rate embedded in consumer, business and financial market expectations.

variables.name: Media conflict attention
variables.description: Intensity of media and public attention on the maritime security episode measured by coverage volume and prominence.

variables.name: Restrictive economic measures intensity
variables.description: Aggregate intensity of economic restriction measures (trade controls, blockades, financial restrictions) affecting maritime-linked commerce.

catalysts.title: U.S. announces Iran bank sanctions
catalysts.description: U.S. to announce targeted banking sanctions limiting Iranian access to international finance, increasing economic pressure on Tehran.
catalysts.rationale: Bessent: U.S. likely to announce Iran bank sanctions this week; Treasury already limiting banks.

catalysts.title: OPEC+ keeps output policy unchanged
catalysts.description: OPEC+ decision to maintain current production policy, leaving supply settings unchanged and limiting near-term additional output.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: OPEC+ likely to keep oil output policy unchanged on Sunday.

catalysts.title: Attacks may intensify after U.S. midterms
catalysts.description: U.S. aides warn Iran-related attacks could intensify following the November midterm elections, raising risk of prolonged escalation.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Trump aides say attacks may intensify after November elections.

catalysts.title: Iran blacklists ships / blockade continues
catalysts.description: Iran expands blacklisting and blockading of vessels transiting Hormuz, detaining or stopping ships and restricting commercial passage.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Iran blacklists more ships; Blockade succeeds where sanctions failed; Iranian media report tanker stopped.

catalysts.title: Mine warfare and mine incidents increase
catalysts.description: Escalation or continued use of naval mines in Hormuz raises mine density and the risk of vessels striking mines, complicating navigation.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Mine Warfare With Iran...' and reports Iran says two tankers hit naval mines.

catalysts.title: Sustained rerouting and ship-to-ship transfers
catalysts.description: Shippers increasingly use ship-to-ship transfers and longer routes around Hormuz, shifting flows and lengthening transit times.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Qatari/UAE LNG ship-to-ship transfers; commentary on longer trade routes.

catalysts.title: Further U.S. kinetic strikes in near term
catalysts.description: Expect additional U.S. strikes on Iranian targets in the coming weeks as tit-for-tat exchanges continue.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: U.S. launches further strikes; Trump vows to hit Iran 'hard' after attacks.
